cards.text: Jesus is still giving John letters for the seven churches, and this next one is for the church in Sardis. He introduces Himself as the One who holds the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. Okay, friend. Lean in.
Jesus tells Sardis He knows their deeds. And this church has a reputation around town.

cards.question: What reputation does the church in Sardis have?
Jesus says the church in Sardis really is what its reputation says.

cards.text: Known for being alive, but Jesus says they're dead. Friend, that's the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, swearing up and down they STILL had a little charge left.

cards.question: Sardis looks alive but is dead. What's the first thing Jesus tells the church in Sardis to do?
Jesus tells Sardis to strengthen what's left, which is about to die, because He found their deeds ___ in the sight of His God.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them to remember what they received and heard, keep it, and repent. And He says wake up AGAIN, so Sardis, this is NOT a snooze-button situation.

cards.question: If the church in Sardis doesn't wake up, how does Jesus say He will come?
Jesus tells the church in Sardis the hour when He will come upon them.

cards.text: But not everybody in Sardis is asleep. Jesus says a few people there have not soiled their garments.

cards.question: Because they are worthy, what does Jesus say those few people in Sardis will do?

cards.text: And it's not only them. Like them, anyone who overcomes will be dressed in white.

cards.question: To the church that looks alive but is dead, Jesus promises He will never blot the overcomer's name out of the Book of ___.
Jesus says He will confess the overcomer's name before His Father and His angels.

cards.text: Then that line again, the one every letter so far has had: "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches."

Next letter goes to the church in Philadelphia. Jesus introduces Himself as the One who is holy and true, who holds the key of David. I shared a drawer with a mystery key that NEVER figured out which door it opened, so friend, I am paying ATTENTION.

cards.question: Jesus holds the key of David. What does He say about the things He opens?

cards.text: Then Jesus tells Philadelphia He knows their deeds. And He has placed something right in front of them.

cards.question: The One with the key of David has placed something before the church in Philadelphia. What is it?
Jesus says the church in Philadelphia has great strength.

cards.text: Only a little strength? Friend, I spent YEARS with blurry edges in the back of a drawer, so I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Even with only a little strength, the church in Philadelphia has kept Jesus' ___ and has not denied His ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks about those who belong to the synagogue of Satan, who claim to be Jews but are liars instead.

cards.question: What does Jesus say He'll make those liars do at the feet of the church in Philadelphia?
Jesus says those liars will know that He loves the church in Philadelphia.

cards.text: Philadelphia kept His command to persevere. Now Jesus talks about an hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world.

cards.question: The church in Philadelphia kept His command to persevere. What does Jesus say He'll do for them about the hour of testing?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "I am coming soon." And Philadelphia has something worth protecting.

cards.question: Jesus tells the church in Philadelphia to hold fast to what they have, so no one will take their ___.

cards.text: Jesus will make the one who overcomes a pillar in the temple of His God, and he will never again leave it. Friend, I spent years in a drawer hoping nobody would clean it out, so that promise gets me RIGHT here.

cards.question: Jesus will write the name of the city of His God on the one who overcomes. Which city?
Jesus says He will also write His own new name on the one who overcomes.

cards.text: Then that line again: "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches." Hang tight, friend, because this message isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus is giving John letters for the seven churches. John and the letters to the seven churches come from outside the passage (Revelation 1:1, 1:11, 1:19-20), and Revelation 3:1 never names John. The card cites only Revelation 3:1, so these outside facts have no reference. John is also never introduced, though this is his first appearance in the lesson.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: John appears without a short description of who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card says every letter so far has had this line. That is true (Revelation 2:7, 2:11, 2:17, 2:29), but those verses are outside the passage, and the card cites only Revelation 3:6. The outside facts need their references.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Revelation 3:12 says Jesus will write three names on the overcomer: the name of His God, the name of the city of His God, and His new name. Cards 16 and 17 cover only the city and the new name. The name of God is never told, and card 17's "also" suggests the list is complete.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The humor relies on one device. Four of the five jokes are the same junk-drawer callback (stop 1 card 5, stop 2 cards 1, 6 and 15). Most other story cards are plain retelling with no reaction or comparison (stop 1 cards 2, 11, 13; stop 2 cards 3, 8, 11, 13). The voice reads as a nice dad being pleasant, not as laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
